objections.claim: The spec's edge-case analysis asserts that a spec whose only non-prose DONE items are code-surface (judged_count 0, integration_count > 0) yields an evaluator block with `criteria: []` that "rolls up to `needs-human` (ADR-0140)". ADR-0140 does not establish this — it addresses prose Scenarios units and the delegated route, never the aggregate derivation over an empty criteria array. The derivation is canonical at `faff contract holdout-verdict --describe`, which is not in evidence, and the evaluator SKILL's `needs-human` + `criteria: []` example is the env-not-ready case, not a derivation rule. If the contract's derivation treats an empty criteria set as vacuously all-met (`meets-spec`), the outcome **does** change: a class of specs this change creates (code-surface-only non-prose DONE) would pass the holdout leg with nothing judged — exactly the vacuous-pass direction the spec's own first design principle ("a false match costs more than a miss") forbids. No scenario in section 5 and no DONE criterion (ac-1..ac-16) exercises the judged_count-0 roll-up; ac-2 tests the 7-judged FAFF-1354 case only.
objections.evidence: section 4 → edge cases, bullet "A spec whose only non-prose items are code-surface DONE items"; section 1 Problem ("Before this change the same spec reached `needs-human` through the judged items, so the outcome does not change"); ADR 0140 (supplied) contains no empty-criteria rule.
objections.predicted_consequence: if the derivation is vacuous-all-met, an integration-only spec's holdout record is accepted (the writer's judged-id check passes trivially on two empty sets) with `aggregate: meets-spec`, the merge floor's holdout leg passes on zero verification, and the regression is invisible because no test covers it.
objections.disposition_rationale: Revision 2 cites the holdout-verdict derivation and adds ac-17.

objections.claim: `buildHoldoutRecord`'s new derivation check is gated on "IF every verdict is one of met | unmet | needs-human", with no stated refusal for the else-branch. A block whose criteria carry a verdict outside that set (e.g. `"pending"`) skips the derivation check entirely, so an aggregate that disagrees with its criteria — or any aggregate at all — is written as-is. The spec's stated purpose for the whole writer change is that "the change moves the refusal to write time and makes the stored record say why"; for the malformed-verdict input class it does the opposite: the block is stored as `meets-spec` and only rejected later by `computeHoldoutVerdict` at the re-validating gates — the exact pre-existing defect the subsection says it eliminates. If `holdoutRecordViolations(redacted)` already refuses invalid verdicts, the spec never says so, and a builder following the pseudocode literally ships the hole.
objections.evidence: section 4, "The record writer refuses an aggregate its criteria do not derive", step 2 ("same guard computeHoldoutVerdict uses" — a guard that skips, not refuses); the subsection's framing "the writer must refuse it … the change moves the refusal to write time".
objections.predicted_consequence: a holdout record with a malformed verdict and a wrong aggregate is written to `.faff/holdout/` as `meets-spec`, passes the writer, and only fails at the next gate that runs `computeHoldoutVerdict` — the late-failure mode this change was added to remove survives for that input class, and ac-18's selftest (which pins only the aggregate-mismatch case) does not catch it.
objections.disposition_rationale: holdoutRecordViolations runs next and the anchored schema allows only met, unmet and needs-human, so the block is refused; a clarifying sentence was added.

objections.claim: The writer's new refusal check is explicitly conditional — it derives the expected aggregate only "IF every verdict is one of met | unmet | needs-human". The evaluator block arrives on stdin (`faff holdout record --issue … --spec …`), i.e. it is untrusted input to a governance-region writer. A block whose criteria carry any other verdict value (a typo, a future tier string, or a deliberately malformed value) skips the derivation check entirely, so an aggregate that disagrees with its criteria — the exact defect this change exists to catch — can still be written, just via a different route than `meets-spec` + `criteria: []`.
objections.evidence: section 4, "The record writer refuses an aggregate its criteria do not derive", step 2: "IF every verdict is one of met | unmet | needs-human: … IF redacted.aggregate != expected: refusals.push(...)". No clause states that the writer refuses (rather than skips derivation for) a block containing an out-of-set verdict.
objections.predicted_consequence: a holdout record is persisted with `aggregate: "meets-spec"` alongside criteria whose verdicts do not derive it; the record is only caught later at re-validation gates (`readHoldout`, `faff holdout verdicts`) — the same deferred-refusal behaviour the spec calls out as the defect being moved to write time. The fix is a one-line edit: refuse any verdict outside the set instead of skipping the derivation.
objections.disposition_rationale: Same as 3#0: the schema check refuses an out-of-set verdict; clarifying sentence added.
